titleEn: Ducks Are Ducks, Dingding Is Dingding!

pages.text: "I want to do that, too!" Dingding stood by the lower paddy, watching ducks float and swim in circles. Mr. Ming, who kept ducks in the lowest paddy, was driving them farther away.
Dingding crouched on the bank and stirred the water with both hands. The ducks floated, but Dingding's hands only splashed. "The ducks are good at it. Why can't I do it?"
A duck darted past. Dingding's shoulders and ears drooped. "I can't swim or quack." Dingding kicked little bits of soil with their toes.
Mr. Ming stopped driving the ducks and crouched beside Dingding. "What's wrong?" "The ducks can swim, and I can't." Dingding looked sad.
"Duck beaks pick things from the water's surface. They can't see inside the mud." Mr. Ming guided Dingding's hand into the soil. Their fingers found something round. A pond snail!

Dingding picked up one, two, three snails and put them on their palm. Even when the ducks gathered, they could not catch the snails hidden in the mud. Mr. Ming sang, "Ducks Are Ducks, Dingding Is Dingding!"
Dingding opened their palm wide to show the ducks. The ducks stretched their necks to look at the snails. Dingding grinned. "Ducks Are Ducks, Dingding Is Dingding!"
Dingding sniffed the rich earthy smell on their hands. Their drooping ears perked up. Dingding was not jealous anymore.
Dingding and Mr. Ming sat beside the paddy and counted together. "One, ducks swim! Two, Mr. Ming drives ducks! Three, Dingding collects pond snails!" Dingding held the snails tightly.

Grandma, who had farmed rice all her life, lifted Dingding into a hug. "We'll make pond-snail soup. You caught them all!" Everyone was good at different things. Dingding called, "Ducks Are Ducks, Dingding Is Dingding!"
